LESSON: SOIL ENVIRONMENT

Grade: PP1
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: NATURAL
Topic 3.5: Soil ENVIRONMENT

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Soil ENVIRONMENT. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when a) talk about the safety with soil playing with soil?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Soil ENVIRONMENT means using everyday Kenyan examples
2. describe how Soil ENVIRONMENT appears at home, school, or in the environment
3. practise one safe skill connected to Soil ENVIRONMENT
4. tell why Soil ENVIRONMENT matters for life in Kenya

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SOIL ENVIRONMENT
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Soil ENVIRONMENT helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: SOIL ENVIRONMENT
Soil ENVIRONMENT is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Explain what Soil ENVIRONMENT means using everyday Kenyan examples

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Soil ENVIRONMENT means using everyday Kenyan examples. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Soil ENVIRONMENT means using everyday Kenyan examples.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil ENVIRONMENT” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Soil ENVIRONMENT means using everyday Kenyan examples. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe how Soil ENVIRONMENT appears at home, school, or in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how Soil ENVIRONMENT appears at home, school, or in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how Soil ENVIRONMENT appears at home, school, or in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Soil ENVIRONMENT matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how Soil ENVIRONMENT appears at home, school, or in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise one safe skill connected to Soil ENVIRONMENT

What this means
In this part you learn to practise one safe skill connected to Soil ENVIRONMENT. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise one safe skill connected to Soil ENVIRONMENT.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Soil ENVIRONMENT this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise one safe skill connected to Soil ENVIRONMENT. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Tell why Soil ENVIRONMENT matters for life in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to tell why Soil ENVIRONMENT matters for life in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: tell why Soil ENVIRONMENT matters for life in Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil ENVIRONMENT” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can tell why Soil ENVIRONMENT matters for life in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Soil ENVIRONMENT is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil ENVIRONMENT” around your school. (skill: explain what Soil ENVIRONMENT means using everyday Kenyan examples)

Example 2: Say why Soil ENVIRONMENT matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe how Soil ENVIRONMENT appears at home, school, or in the environment)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Soil ENVIRONMENT this week. (skill: practise one safe skill connected to Soil ENVIRONMENT)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil ENVIRONMENT” around your school. (skill: tell why Soil ENVIRONMENT matters for life in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Soil ENVIRONMENT to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Soil ENVIRONMENT means using everyday Kenyan examples.
3. Practise this skill: describe how Soil ENVIRONMENT appears at home, school, or in the environment.
4. Practise this skill: practise one safe skill connected to Soil ENVIRONMENT.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Soil ENVIRONMENT from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Soil ENVIRONMENT: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Soil ENVIRONMENT?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when a) talk about the safety with soil playing with soil?
2. when do when playing with • learners tell safety measures soil?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Soil ENVIRONMENT means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Soil ENVIRONMENT means using everyday Kenyan examples.
5. Be able to: describe how Soil ENVIRONMENT appears at home, school, or in the environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
